probes.support_reason: PARTIAL under P-a (R9 substitution exception, which this probe's canonical_task names explicitly). Sub-requirement (1) asks for storage whose contents are NOT specified to be zero or any other value. Kotlin has no documented mechanism for obtaining uninitialized bulk storage: every array constructor and factory in kotlin-stdlib specifies the contents. The dispositive citation is the frozen toolchain's own stdlib source, kotlin-stdlib 2.3.21 kotlin/UByteArray.kt: '/** Creates a new array of the specified [size], with all elements initialized to zero. */ public constructor(size: Int)'; the same holds for ByteArray, and `arrayOfNulls` specifies null. Kotlin/JVM inherits the JVM rule that a newly created array is initialized to the default value for its element type (JVMS 21, 2.9 / newarray), so no Kotlin expression can produce genuinely indeterminate bulk storage. The probe therefore takes the named substitution: the default-initialized 16-element buffer is written and measured. Sub-requirements (2) and (3) ARE delivered in full: `buf[0] = 1u` writes the value 1 into element 0 and `return buf[0]` reads it back; the program prints 1. The element type is the exact one the task names - UByte is Kotlin's unsigned 8-bit integer - so no weakening of the element type was taken. Observed on the frozen toolchain and disclosed in full: the buffer is zero-filled (witness /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-koba-Desktop-Quidra/c7dc7758-3bc7-4b38-ac54-4af31eae0682/scratchpad/bench/quidra-scratch/benchmark/2026-09-17-7677581/semantic-compression/probes/witnesses/F02.P2/kotlin/OBS_zero_filled_and_oob/w.kt prints 'zero-filled: 0,0,0,...,0'), which is the direct evidence that Kotlin gives default-initialized, not uninitialized, storage. Its usage should be marked with @kotlin.ExperimentalUnsignedTypes or @OptIn(kotlin.ExperimentalUnsignedTypes::class)'. The build succeeds with warnings only and needs no flag beyond the frozen recipe, but that wording would independently engage F-6's 'unstable'-equivalent test and rubric condition P-d. Per the rubric's no_double_penalty_rule the applicable letters are recorded (P-a, and P-d in the alternative) and the factor remains a single 0.5.
